insights.body: In DE, 17.2% of installs now turn into new subs — -18.5% versus last period. It is about 7% of revenue (a market worth watching): fewer of the people downloading are subscribing, and revenue will feel that within a week or two.

insights.title: Revenue vs new subs — App Total Revenue -6.6% matches the new subs signed up 7 days earlier.
insights.body: App Total Revenue on 09-03 vs 08-27 is -6.6%, and App Total New Subs on 08-27 vs 08-20 was -3.8% — both moved the same way. Most new subs start as a 7-day free trial, so the revenue landing now mostly comes from people who subscribed about 7 days ago. This is the normal pattern, so no surprise is building up.

insights.title: Best and worst markets — GB turns installs into new subs best of anywhere (21.3% vs 12.2% overall).
insights.body: In GB, 21.3% of installs turn into new subs, versus 12.2% across all markets and apps (+9.1pp difference). That is much better than the rest — worth understanding and copying. GB is about 4% of revenue. Its App Total New Subs is -12.4% this period.

insights.title: Next period outlook — No big App Total Revenue swing expected in about 7 days — the share of installs that become subs is normal.
insights.body: App Total New Subs is -10.0% and App Total Install is -6.2%; the gap between them (-3.8pp) is under the 10pp we treat as a real signal, so the share of people who install and then subscribe is close to normal. New subs start as 7-day free trials, so today's new subs are next period's App Total Revenue. So nothing unusual is building up that would swing App Total Revenue in about 7 days.
